summary.prose: Correct design artifact relevance guidance across author, builder and reviewer prompts, with no schema changes. Isolated class implementation changes that do not affect relationships need no ERD. Relationship changes, even simple ones, must document endpoints, direction, cardinality/ownership and compatibility where applicable; use a concise table/text for a clearly understandable change or an ERD when it materially clarifies the model. Sequence/component diagrams explain interaction or boundary changes; UX mocks explain changed layouts, states or flows. Reviewers independently assess necessity even when no definition is supplied, inspect generated links/files/rendered content and consistency, and report unavailable rendering honestly. Advisory means narrative advice, NOT a warn verdict or a does-not-hold/LOW finding. Keep existing verdict semantics unchanged: confirmed material inadequacy is does-not-hold with MED/HIGH and blocks; genuinely unavailable evidence is could-not-verify and warns; an adequate design can hold with optional improvement advice in evidence/action. Never label a confirmed failure unverified or assert a missing artifact exists. An optional visual not required for assessment is not a failed requirement. Missing relationship documentation remains a defect even when no diagram is needed. Builders maintain relevant artifacts when implementation changes the approved relationships/UX, without inventing scope. This prompt-only change itself needs no visual artifact.
